title: FTC Probes Block After Consumer Complaints Over Frozen Accounts
summary: The Federal Trade Commission is investigating whether Block Inc., the parent of Square and Cash App, violated US consumer protection laws by failing to provide adequate customer service to help with frozen or deactivated accounts amid significant cuts in staffing.

title: Oracle Moves Gas by Trucks to Avoid Data Center Power Delays
summary: Oracle Corp. is using a novel power strategy to keep several data centers on track: trucking natural gas directly to the server farms.

title: Musk Asks If Ambani Is ‘Real Boss of India’ in Fresh Jibe
summary: Elon Musk stepped up his criticism of Indian rivals with a direct swipe at billionaire Mukesh Ambani, as SpaceX’s Starlink satellite broadband network continues to await regulatory approval for a rollout in the country.

title: Inside John Ternus’ New Apple + Meta’s Vision Pro Killer
summary:
In this episode of Power On, Mark Gurman and Bloomberg tech editor Vlad Savov unpack John Ternus’ first month running Apple — from his push to make the company leaner and faster to his unusually hands-on role overseeing design. They discuss why more layoffs could be coming, how Ternus is putting design back at the center of Apple and why Tim Cook, now executive chairman, remains the company’s face on the world stage. Then, Mark gives his verdict on Meta’s new $1,299 VR glasses after trying them himself — and explains why they are the device Apple’s Vision Pro should have been all along.

title: Apple Announces Oct. 13 Smart Home Product Launch in New York
summary: Apple Inc. on Thursday confirmed it will hold an Oct. 13 product launch in New York to introduce new smart home products.

title: Britain’s Great Wealth Dilemma
summary: Individuals behind a combined $160 billion are leaving London as UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham tries to balance tax fairness with revenue. The exodus has raised questions about the city’s status as a wealth hub. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: AI Model Evaluator Arena Valued at Over $3 Billion in Round
summary: Arena Intelligence Inc., the startup behind a popular artificial intelligence model leaderboard, has raised $200 million in funding at a $3.1 billion valuation and plans to expand into measuring AI safety, tapping into growing demand to evaluate the technology’s performance and risks.The financing, set to be announced Thursday, was led by Lightspeed Venture Partners and Khosla Ventures, with participation from Salesforce Ventures and Dell Technologies Capital. title: Nigeria-Founded Moove to Exit Country After Uber Pulled Out
summary: Moove, the Nigerian-founded mobility startup valued at $2.1 billion, plans to exit the African country after Uber Technologies Inc. closed its operations in early September.

title: CreditSights' Cisar Sees Cracks in AI Credit Boom
summary: Winnie Cisar, global head of strategy at CreditSights, says the surge in AI financing is making credit analysis increasingly difficult as investors weigh uncertain returns, potential data center overbuilding and more complex financing structures. She speaks on "Bloomberg Surveillance." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: GlobalFoundries Rallies After Announcing $2 Billion TSMC Deal
summary: GlobalFoundries Inc. shares gained as much as 7% after the chip manufacturer announced a five-year, $2 billion deal to provide US production capacity to Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co.

title: What Everyone Gets Wrong About the Economic Problems in Europe
summary: It has been two years since the publication of the Draghi report and the problems the report identified about European competitiveness are far from solved: Demographic challenges, rising energy costs, and a lagging tech sector still cast a shadow over Europe. But according to the economist and policy analyst Dominik Leusder (who also writes the Leusder of Last Resort Substack) the Draghi report might have mismeasured the true scale of Europe's issues, and he asks if the popular narrative of European decline is an accurate one. We also speak about whether Europe needs a frontier AI model, why long, wine-soaked lunches are not a good way to measure productivity, and the state of Europe's vexed relationship with China as a trade partner and competitor. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Former OpenAI, Cognition Staffers Want AI to Help Run a Business

title: Ellison Family Invests About $17 Billion in Warner Bros. Takeover
summary: David Ellison and his family invested approximately $17 billion to complete Paramount Skydance’s acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery, according to public filings. Dylan Sloan reports on "Bloomberg Open Interest." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Google Launches Workplace AI Agent That Acts Like Colleague
summary: Alphabet Inc.’s Google announced a Gemini agent for the workplace, ramping up competition with OpenAI, Anthropic PBC and Microsoft Corp. for corporate customers.

title: Broadcom in Early Financing Talks for OpenAI Chips
summary: Broadcom is planning its next blockbuster deal after launching a $60 billion debt financing to help fund Anthropic PBC's artificial intelligence build-out. Sarah Frier has more on "Bloomberg Open Interest." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Singapore’s Wong Warns AI Tech Rally Faces Eventual Correction
summary: Singapore Prime Minister Lawrence Wong cautioned that the global tech rally powering regional economic growth will inevitably face a market correction, saying his government intends to capitalize on the current window of opportunity before trade momentum cools.

title: SK Hynix’s Solidigm Is Said to Pick Banks for US IPO Next Year
summary: SK Hynix Inc.’s Solidigm has picked lead banks for its US initial public offering next year, according to people familiar with the matter.

title: OpenAI Investment Boosts Tiger Global's Hedge Fund
summary: OpenAI is in talks to raise $30 billion at a $1.4 trillion valuation, with Tiger Global poised for a paper profit of $5 billion. Hema Parmar reports on "Bloomberg Open Interest." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Apple Watch Series 12, Ultra 4 New Features Aren't Enough to Beat Oura, Whoop
summary: New Apple Health features narrow the gap, but people who are serious about fitness shouldn't ditch their purpose-built health trackers yet.

title: Union Square Ventures Doubles Fund Size, Shrinks Team for AI Era
summary: New York City-based venture firm Union Square Ventures is reinventing itself to better compete in the artificial intelligence race by nearly doubling the size of its core fund and whittling down its general partnership to just four investors.
